meaning.en: Bad blood means lasting anger, dislike, resentment or hostility between two people or groups, usually because they argued or treated each other badly in the past.
meaning.zh: Bad blood 指兩個人或群體之間持續存在的憤怒、不滿、怨恨或敵意，通常源於過往的爭執或不愉快事件。

register.summaryEn: sports reports; workplace discussions; stories about family or friendship problems; general writing about conflict.
register.summaryZh: Bad blood 屬中性表達，但所表達的情緒較強烈。 它適合用於日常對話、新聞、體育報道、工作討論，以及有關家庭、友誼或群體衝突的一般文章。
contextsEn: stories about family or friendship problems
register.formalEn: In very formal writing, hostility, resentment, conflict or strained relations may sometimes be more suitable.
register.formalZh: 在非常正式的文章中，有時可使用 hostility、resentment、conflict 或 strained relations。

benefits.titleEn: It Describes More Than One Argument
benefits.titleZh: 形容爭執留下的長期影響
benefits.en: Bad blood does not focus only on the original argument. It describes the hostility that remains afterwards.
benefits.zh: 不只集中於原本的爭執，還形容爭執過後仍然存在的敵意。 兩名鄰居自去年起一直存在積怨。

examples.en: There has been bad blood between the two neighbours since last year.
examples.zh: 兩名鄰居自去年起一直存在積怨。

benefits.en: The expression explains the hidden relationship behind the visible problem.
benefits.zh: 兩個團隊之間的積怨令合作變得困難。 這個表達能夠解釋表面問題背後的緊張關係。

examples.en: The bad blood between the teams made cooperation difficult.
examples.zh: 兩個團隊之間的積怨令合作變得困難。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Describe Cause, Development and Result
benefits.titleZh: 可以形容成因、發展及結果
benefits.en: The bad blood made cooperation difficult.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以用於說明積怨的成因、發展及所造成的結果。

benefits.titleZh: 可以自然地否認不和傳聞
benefits.en: This is a concise way to say that two people do not seriously resent each other.
benefits.zh: 我們之間沒有任何芥蒂。 這是一種簡潔的說法，表示雙方並沒有嚴重怨恨對方。

examples.en: There is no bad blood between us.
examples.zh: 我們之間沒有任何芥蒂。

benefits.en: the main noun after there is; the subject of a sentence; the object after cause or create; a noun phrase after because of or despite; part of a question or negative statement.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以置於 there is 之後、作為句子主語、置於 cause 或 create 之後作賓語、置於 because of 或 despite 之後，亦可以用於疑問句或否定句。

origin.statusEn: Gradual Development; Exact First Use Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切首次用法未能完全確定

history.en: Merriam-Webster records 1664 as its first known use of bad blood in the sense of ill feeling or bitterness. Some other dictionary histories date the familiar modern form to the early nineteenth century. These different dates probably reflect differences in which early examples and forms each dictionary accepts.
history.zh: Merriam-Webster 把 bad blood 表示不和或怨恨的最早已知用法追溯至1664年。 部分其他字典則把人們熟悉的現代形式追溯至十九世紀初。 這些日期不同，很可能是因為各字典對早期例子及表達形式採用了不同判斷標準。

history.en: Over time, bad blood stopped being understood mainly as something physically wrong inside a person. It became a conventional image for hostility existing between people or groups.
history.zh: 隨着時間發展，bad blood 不再主要被理解為某人體內出現問題，而逐漸成為形容人或群體之間存在敵意的固定意象。

origin.memoryEn: An old conflict leaves bad feelings flowing between two sides.
origin.memoryZh: 過往的衝突令負面情緒持續存在於雙方之間。

rules.titleEn: Keep the Two Fixed Words Together
rules.titleZh: 規則一：兩個固定字詞不可分開
rules.en: Keep the Two Fixed Words Together
rules.zh: 兩個固定字詞不可分開

rules.titleEn: Do Not Add an Indefinite Article
rules.titleZh: 規則二：不要在前面加入不定冠詞
rules.en: Do Not Add an Indefinite Article
rules.zh: 不要在前面加入不定冠詞

rules.titleZh: 規則三：使用 between 指出雙方
rules.en: Between is part of the surrounding grammar, not part of the fixed expression.
rules.zh: Between 屬於句子的外圍結構，並不是慣用語的固定部分。

rules.titleZh: 規則四：用於持續的敵意
rules.zh: 兩名表親自去年爭吵後一直存在嫌隙。 露西因諾亞遲到五分鐘而有點不滿。

examples.en: There has been bad blood between the cousins since their argument last year.
examples.zh: 兩名表親自去年爭吵後一直存在嫌隙。

examples.en: This brief annoyance does not normally justify bad blood.
examples.zh: 露西因諾亞遲到五分鐘而有點不滿。

rules.titleEn: A Past Cause Is Usually Present
rules.titleZh: 規則五：通常存在過往成因
rules.en: an argument; an unfair decision; an accusation; competition; betrayal; blame; money; an old family problem.
rules.zh: 常見成因包括爭執、不公平決定、指控、競爭、背叛、責怪、金錢問題及過往的家庭衝突。

rules.titleZh: 規則六：不要按字面解釋
rules.en: In this exercise, blood does not refer to the red liquid inside the body. The doctor tested the patient’s blood.
rules.zh: 在本練習中，blood 並不是指身體內的血液。 醫生化驗病人的血液。 醫生與前經理之間存在積怨。

examples.en: There is bad blood between the doctor and the former manager.
examples.zh: 醫生與前經理之間存在積怨。

rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possibility into a certainty.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把「可能」改成「肯定」，改變了原句的確定程度。

rules.titleZh: 規則九：No Bad Blood 表示沒有積怨
rules.en: This does not mean the people are close friends. It only denies serious resentment or hostility.
rules.zh: 我們之間沒有芥蒂。 這不代表雙方一定是親密朋友，只是否認彼此存在嚴重積怨或敵意。

examples.en: There is no bad blood between us.
examples.zh: 我們之間沒有芥蒂。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Force It into Every Disagreement
rules.titleZh: 規則十：不要用於每一項意見分歧
rules.en: Two people may disagree politely without developing bad blood.
rules.zh: 兩個人可以禮貌地持不同意見，而不一定因此產生積怨。
